title: The LJ disjunction-left diagram repeats its first disjunct.
details: Baelde, June 2013, §1.5 Definition 12, printed p. 16 (PDF p. 17), displays both premises of disjunction-left as Γ,A0 ⊢ P. The second must be Γ,A1 ⊢ P. Taken literally the displayed rule is unsound: choose empty Γ, A0=P=p and A1=q; two copies of p ⊢ p would yield p∨q ⊢ p, refuted by p=false,q=true. The ordinary distinct-branch rule in §1.2 identifies the intended correction, which preserves the stated constructive calculus. The planned intuitionistic sequent entry uses the corrected rule; it does not claim an upstream correction. Current corpus adoption: intuitionistic-propositional-sequents#disjunction-rules. The entry uses the checked correction; no upstream correction is inferred.
